alternate-lookup-span-key.title: Look up Dictionary entries with alternate Span keys
alternate-lookup-span-key.short: Search without constructing the dictionary's key type first.
alternate-lookup-span-key.summary: Dictionary.GetAlternateLookup<TAlternateKey> can query a dictionary with another key representation when its comparer supports that alternate type.
alternate-lookup-span-key.why: For frequent ReadOnlySpan<char> lookups into string-keyed dictionaries, this can avoid allocating a temporary string for each query.
alternate-lookup-span-key.tips: The comparer must support the requested alternate key type. Prefer ordinary TryGetValue when allocation is not a meaningful concern.

memoryextensions-split-span.title: Split text as spans with MemoryExtensions.Split
memoryextensions-split-span.short: Enumerate field ranges without allocating many substrings.
memoryextensions-split-span.summary: Span-oriented Split can expose separated fields as ranges so each field can be processed while still referring to the original data.
memoryextensions-split-span.why: Parsing logs or delimiter-separated input can avoid the many substring allocations commonly produced by string.Split.
memoryextensions-split-span.tips: The ranges refer to the original input. Convert only values that must be retained beyond that input's lifetime.

readexactly-stream.title: Use Stream.ReadExactlyAsync for fixed-length data
readexactly-stream.short: Keep reading until the requested buffer is full.
readexactly-stream.summary: ReadExactlyAsync fills the supplied buffer and reports an unexpected end of stream instead of silently returning a shorter fixed-length value.
readexactly-stream.why: Stream.ReadAsync is allowed to return fewer bytes than requested, so one read is not sufficient for protocol headers and other fixed-size records.
readexactly-stream.tips: Use this where the format requires an exact size; ordinary end-of-stream processing should continue to use normal read loops.

writeallbytesasync-memory.title: Write ReadOnlyMemory<byte> directly with File.WriteAllBytesAsync
writeallbytesasync-memory.short: Write an existing memory buffer to a whole file asynchronously.
writeallbytesasync-memory.summary: The ReadOnlyMemory<byte> overload of File.WriteAllBytesAsync can write memory-backed data without first converting it to a new byte array.
writeallbytesasync-memory.why: Code that already stores data in Memory-based buffers can avoid an otherwise unnecessary conversion solely for file output.
writeallbytesasync-memory.tips: For very large or incrementally produced data, write chunks through FileStream instead. Pass cancellation when the operation should be interruptible.

task-delay-timeprovider.title: Pass TimeProvider to Task.Delay for testable delays
task-delay-timeprovider.short: Avoid coupling delay logic directly to real elapsed time.
task-delay-timeprovider.summary: The TimeProvider-aware Task.Delay overload lets delay behavior use an injected time source rather than always depending on the system's real clock.
task-delay-timeprovider.why: Tests for retries and timeouts become slow and fragile when they must wait for real time, while an injectable time source can make them deterministic.
task-delay-timeprovider.tips: Using one injected TimeProvider for both time reads and delays keeps an application's time-dependent behavior consistent.

periodic-timer-wait.title: Make PeriodicTimer loops testable with TimeProvider
periodic-timer-wait.short: Drive recurring async work from an injected time source.
periodic-timer-wait.summary: The TimeProvider-aware PeriodicTimer constructor lets a periodic async loop use the same replaceable time source as the rest of testable time-dependent code.
periodic-timer-wait.why: Tests for polling or maintenance loops should not need to wait for real wall-clock ticks when the application's time source can be controlled.
periodic-timer-wait.tips: Keep cancellation and disposal explicit, and decide how slow iterations should behave when multiple timer periods elapse before the next wait.

jsonnode-mutable-dom.title: Modify JSON as a mutable tree with JsonNode
jsonnode-mutable-dom.short: Parse JSON, change selected nodes, and serialize it again.
jsonnode-mutable-dom.summary: JsonNode provides a mutable JSON DOM whose object and array elements can be read and replaced before producing updated JSON.
jsonnode-mutable-dom.why: It is useful for configuration-like documents where only a few values need changing and defining a complete strongly typed model would add little value.
jsonnode-mutable-dom.tips: Compare JsonDocument for read-only traversal and JsonSerializer when the document maps naturally to known .NET types.

regex-enumeratematches-span.title: Reduce match allocations with Regex.EnumerateMatches
regex-enumeratematches-span.short: Enumerate match ranges without creating Match objects.
regex-enumeratematches-span.summary: EnumerateMatches reports Span-based matches as ValueMatch values whose Index and Length can address the matching region of the original input.
regex-enumeratematches-span.why: When code only scans many matches, avoiding a Match object for every result can reduce allocation overhead.
regex-enumeratematches-span.tips: Use the regular Match APIs when you need richer information such as Groups or Captures.

linq-countby.title: Count occurrences per key with CountBy
linq-countby.short: Express frequency counting directly instead of grouping then counting.
linq-countby.summary: Enumerable.CountBy selects a key for each element and enumerates key/count pairs representing how often each key occurred.
linq-countby.why: For frequency tables, it states the operation more directly than GroupBy followed only by Count for every group.
linq-countby.tips: The result is evaluated when enumerated. Materialize it into a Dictionary or another collection when repeated access is required.

linq-aggregateby.title: Aggregate values per key with AggregateBy
linq-aggregateby.short: Build a running aggregate independently for each key.
linq-aggregateby.summary: Enumerable.AggregateBy applies an initial accumulator and aggregation function per key, producing grouped totals or other accumulated state.
linq-aggregateby.why: It directly represents per-key aggregation without first creating GroupBy groupings and then aggregating every group separately.
linq-aggregateby.tips: Choose the overload that fits how each accumulator is initialized, and avoid accidentally sharing mutable accumulator state between keys.
